questions.statement: Bogotá is usually ________ than Cartagena, especially in the early morning.

options.feedback: Incorrect. We need the comparative form.
Correct! For short adjectives, we add "-er" for comparison.
Incorrect. Short adjectives don't use "more".
Incorrect. This is the superlative form, used for more than two things.

questions.explanation:
Para adjetivos cortos (una sílaba), formamos el comparativo agregando el sufijo "-er" seguido de "than".

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Mount Everest is ________ mountain in the world.
questions.context: Expressing the highest quality in a group.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Needs the superlative suffix.
Incorrect. This is for comparing two things.
Correct! Use "the" + "-est" for the superlative of short adjectives.
Incorrect. Short adjectives don't use "most".

questions.explanation:
El superlativo se usa para indicar que algo posee una cualidad en el grado máximo dentro de un grupo. Para adjetivos cortos, usamos "the" y el sufijo "-est".

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: In my opinion, playing the piano is ________ than playing the drums.

options.feedback: Incorrect. "Difficult" is a long adjective.
Correct! Long adjectives use "more" for comparison.
Incorrect. Needs "as" after the adjective to complete the structure.
Incorrect. This is a superlative, not a comparison between two.

questions.explanation:
Para adjetivos largos (de tres o más sílabas), el comparativo se forma anteponiendo la palabra "more" al adjetivo.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: My English grades are ________ this term than they were last year. I am studying harder!

options.feedback: Incorrect. "Good" is an irregular adjective.
Correct! "Better" is the comparative form of "good".
Incorrect. This is the superlative form.
Incorrect. "Good" does not use "more".

questions.explanation:
Algunos adjetivos son irregulares y cambian su forma completamente. El comparativo de "good" es "better" y el de "bad" es "worse".

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: This new smartphone is ________ expensive ________ the previous model. They cost exactly the same.

options.feedback: Correct! We use "as + adjective + as" to show equality.
Incorrect. This would mean they don't cost the same.
Incorrect. This structure is for consequence, not comparison.
Incorrect. This means it is cheaper, but they cost the same.

questions.explanation:
Para comparar dos cosas que son iguales en una cualidad, utilizamos la estructura "as + adjetivo + as" (tan... como).

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Traveling by "Chiva" is definitely ________ than traveling by a modern intercity bus.
questions.context: Comparing traditional and modern transport in Colombia.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Comparative needed.
Correct! Comparison of two modes of transport.
Incorrect. Superlative doesn't fit a comparison between two items.
Incorrect. "Slow" is a short adjective.

questions.explanation:
Al comparar dos elementos específicos (Chiva vs. Bus moderno), debemos usar el grado comparativo. "Slow" es corto, por lo que usamos "-er".

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: There are ________ students in the classroom today than yesterday because of the strike.

options.feedback: Incorrect. "Students" is countable.
Correct! Use "fewer" for countable nouns in comparison.
Incorrect. Not a correct structure.
Incorrect. Superlative form.

questions.explanation:
Aunque en lenguaje informal se usa "less" para todo, gramaticalmente en nivel B1 se distingue entre "less" (para incontables) y "fewer" (para contables como "students").

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement:
"Cali is **by far** the warmest city I have visited in Colombia."
What does "by far" emphasize?

options.text: Cali is a little bit warmer than other cities.
options.feedback: Incorrect. "By far" shows a large difference.

options.text: Cali is much warmer than all the other cities.
options.feedback: Correct! "By far" emphasizes a significant difference in a superlative.
Incorrect. It says the opposite.

options.text: The speaker doesn't like warm cities.
options.feedback: Incorrect. It's a statement of fact, not preference.

questions.explanation:
La expresión "by far" se utiliza con superlativos para enfatizar que la diferencia entre el primer lugar y los demás es muy grande.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: The ________ you study, the ________ your results will be.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Second part must be a comparative too.
Correct! Double comparative structure "The + comparative, the + comparative".
Incorrect. Doesn't follow the correlative structure.
Incorrect. Uses superlatives instead of comparatives.

questions.explanation:
La estructura "The + comparativo..., the + comparativo..." se usa para mostrar cómo una situación depende de otra (Cuanto más..., mejor...).

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which of the following sentences is grammatically **incorrect**?

options.text: This exam was far more difficult than I expected.
options.feedback: Incorrect. This sentence is correct; "far" modifies the comparative.

options.text: She is the least ambitious person in the whole team.
options.feedback: Incorrect. This sentence is correct; "the least" is a negative superlative.

options.text: My house is more bigger than yours.
options.feedback: Correct! This is an error. We should never use "more" with an "-er" comparative.

options.text: Gold is much heavier than aluminum.
options.feedback: Incorrect. This sentence is correct.

questions.explanation:
Un error común que se debe evitar en nivel B1 es la "doble comparación" (usar *more* y el sufijo *-er* al mismo tiempo).

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement:
Compare these two sentences:
1. "The movie was not as good as the book."
2. "The book was better than the movie."

Are they expressing the same idea?

options.text: Yes, both sentences mean the book is superior to the movie.
options.feedback: Correct! "Not as... as" is often a softer way to say "less than".

options.text: No, sentence 1 means they are equal.
options.feedback: Incorrect. "Not as...as" shows inequality.

options.text: No, sentence 2 means the movie is better.
options.feedback: Incorrect. It says the book is better.

options.text: Yes, both sentences mean the movie is the best.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Both favor the book.

questions.explanation:
El estudiante debe reconocer que "not as + adjetivo + as" es una estructura alternativa para expresar inferioridad, equivalente a "less than" o al comparativo opuesto.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement:
"After visiting many places in Colombia, I can say that Medellín has a great climate, but Manizales offers the most breathtaking views of the coffee region."
Choose the best follow-up sentence:
questions.context: Writing a concluding sentence for a travel blog.

options.text: Ultimately, choosing between them depends on whether you prefer warmth or scenery.
options.feedback: Correct! It summarizes the comparison fairly.

options.text: Therefore, Medellín is worse than Manizales in every aspect.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Too extreme and doesn't reflect the original text.

options.text: However, both cities are the most expensive in the world.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Irrelevant to the previous comparison of climate/views.

options.text: I will never go to those places because they are far.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Contradicts the context of having already visited them.

questions.explanation: La creación de una conclusión requiere integrar la información comparativa previa y ofrecer una síntesis equilibrada que respete los matices de la opinión expresada.
